# Citi to acquire rewards platform Kard to power personalized card offers

● 2 hours ago

Citi to acquire rewards platform Kard to power personalized card offers

**What's the deal?** [Citi](https://app.dealroom.co/companies/citicorp) 's US Consumer Cards business has agreed to acquire [Kard Financial](https://app.dealroom.co/companies/nancypickard) , a commerce media and rewards platform that helps banks and fintechs deliver personalized offers. Terms were not disclosed, and Citi said they are not material to its financial results.

**What does [Kard](https://app.dealroom.co/companies/kard_) do?** The company connects financial institutions and merchants using verified transaction data and merchant-funded rewards.

...

**What's next?** The transaction is subject to customary closing conditions. Citi and Kard will continue to operate independently until it closes. [Keefe, Bruyette & Woods](https://app.dealroom.co/companies/keefe_bruyette_woods) advised Kard, while [Sullivan & Cromwell](https://app.dealroom.co/companies/sullivan_cromwell) counseled Citi and [Latham & Watkins](https://app.dealroom.co/companies/latham_watkins) counseled Kard.

**The signal:** Card issuers are increasingly treating rewards as a data-driven commerce channel, not just a perk. By bringing Kard's merchant-funded offers in-house, Citi is betting that personalized loyalty can deepen engagement across both its cardholders and the brands trying to reach them.

_Image credit: Aranami_

* **Key insight** : Citi has agreed to acquire rewards fintech Kard Financial for an undisclosed amount.
* **What's at stake** : Citi's pending purchase of the rewards fintech marks a pivot in the way the $2.9 trillion-asset bank thinks about its points program and comes as interchange continues to come under fire.
* **Expert quote** : "Citi's acquisition of Kard will strengthen its cards business by enabling dynamic, highly targeted merchant-funded ads, rewards, and promotions," Eric Grover, principal, Intrepid Ventures.

At Citi's Investor Day in May, U.S. Head of Consumer Cards [Pam Habner](https://www.americanbanker.
com/news/2025-the-most-powerful-women-in-banking-no-22-pam-habner-citigroup) took the stage and said the $2.9 trillion-asset bank and the third largest credit card issuer in the country was going to reduce its dependency on "expensive, points-based rewards." On Thursday, it took a step toward that goal.

Processing Content

Citi agreed to acquire New York-based commerce media and rewards fintech Kard Financial for an undisclosed amount. Kard uses predictive artificial intelligence and first-party transaction data to offer customers personalized, merchant-funded rewards.

Kard will enable Citi to use verified transaction data, machine learning-powered matching and an expanded network of merchant relationships to improve incentive marketing, according to Abhinav Anand, Citi's head of value cards, lending and commerce.
"Kard adds advanced personalization capabilities that can identify spending patterns and match customers with relevant offers in real time," Citi's Anand told American Banker. "This will help Citi present more tailored rewards based on actual purchase behavior, while also giving brands and merchants a direct way to reach high-intent consumers."

The acquisition is a signal that Citi is serious about pivoting on its points program, according to Phil Philliou, a payments industry consultant.

"Rewards points programs are a direct cost center that Citi funds as opposed to merchant-funded, offer-based rewards that shift that cost to brands who want targeted access to Citi's 70 million cardmembers," Phillou told American Banker. "It's exciting to see non-points based programs such as merchant-funded offers, gamification, and sweepstakes serving as ways to reward customers and influence spending behavior."

# Citi to acquire Kard, an Underscore VC portfolio company

August 14, 2026

![](https://luyawlnnudilfvtgkrmk.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/news-images/thumbs/citi-to-acquire-kard.jpg)

Citi (NYSE: C) announced on August 13, 2026 that its U.S. Consumer Cards business has entered into an agreement to acquire Kard Financial, Inc., a New York-based company that operates a commerce media and rewards platform for banks and fintechs. Boston-based Underscore VC led Kard's seed round in 2020 and is among the company's listed investors, alongside Fin Capital and Tiger Global.

Kard connects financial institutions and merchants through verified transaction data and merchant-funded rewards. Its API-driven platform uses machine learning to match offers to individual cardholders, allowing issuers to run personalized rewards programs without building merchant relationships themselves, and giving brands a way to reach consumers based on actual spending behavior.
Citi said the acquisition will combine its scale and payments expertise with Kard's technology, team, and merchant relationships to strengthen its commerce ecosystem. Abhinav Anand, Citi's Head of Value Cards, Lending and Commerce, said Kard's capabilities complement the bank's view of the future of commerce and loyalty and would let it deliver more personalized experiences to customers while creating new ways for brands and merchants to reach consumers. Citi framed the move as advancing priorities set out at its Investor Day.

Kard founder and CEO Ben Mackinnon said joining Citi opens a new chapter for the company and its customers, and that the deal accelerates his original goal of building more rewarding experiences for consumers. Citi reported approximately 70 million cardmembers as of December 31, 2025, across general purpose and private label credit cards and installment lending, primarily in the United States.
Terms of the transaction were not disclosed, and Citi said they are not material to its financial results. The deal is subject to satisfaction of customary closing conditions, and the two companies will continue to operate independently until it closes. Keefe, Bruyette & Woods, a Stifel company, acted as exclusive financial advisor to Kard. Sullivan & Cromwell LLP acted as counsel to Citi, and Latham & Watkins LLP acted as counsel to Kard.

Kard was founded by Mackinnon and is headquartered in New York. Underscore VC led the company's $6.5 million seed financing in 2020 and participated in a $23 million Series A in April 2022 that was led by Tiger Global, with Fin Capital and s12f also taking part. Kard added $15 million in growth capital from Trinity Capital in October 2025.
